company_items.summary: AutoZone reported FQ4 EPS of $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point gross margin tailwind from tariff refunds and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit. Domestic comps missed at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex deeper into the Physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll posted FQ1 EPS of 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even without the tariff refund tailwind of 11 cents — putting the clean beat at 42 cents vs. 36 cents. Sales fell short, down 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while EPS guidance was held unchanged at $1.85–2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The leadership change is an organizational development rather than a financial catalyst.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS expectations, reporting 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% — well below the Street's 13.85% estimate — despite revenue coming in slightly above consensus at $2.311 billion vs. $2.17 billion expected. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressures squeezing household budgets and keeping retail soft, and flagged rising material costs as a significant margin headwind. Some bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost actions underway, and a surge of roughly 75% year-over-year in North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, which demonstrated 22% weight loss in trial participants. The result is a significant milestone for the company's obesity pipeline and positions VK2735 competitively in the rapidly growing GLP-1 market. This is a major positive catalyst for the stock.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday, September 22nd — no broad macro or Fed commentary in today's note, so let's go straight to the names.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat fiscal fourth quarter earnings — fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the Street at fifty-four dollars and three cents. But here's the catch: the beat was low quality. A one hundred forty-five basis point gross margin tailwind from tariff refunds and a one hundred five basis point non-cash LIFO benefit did the heavy lifting. Strip those out and the picture gets messier. Domestic comps came in at plus one point six percent — the Street wanted plus three point one. Operating expenses as a percent of sales rose one hundred basis points year-over-year. Management did flag improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and said they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 growth. Mixed result overall — the headline beat, the quality did not.

Cognex is making a significant move into Physical AI. The company announced an acquisition of RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception — for roughly five hundred million dollars upfront plus another hundred and six and a half million. RealSense is on track to generate eighty to ninety million in revenue, growing more than fifty percent year-over-year. This is a strategic bet on the robotics and Physical AI wave — bullish for Cognex's long-term positioning.

MillerKnoll delivered a clean earnings beat. Fifty-three cents versus the Street at thirty-six cents — and even backing out the eleven-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still beat at forty-two cents clean. The weakness was on the top line — sales down three point three percent organically to nine twenty-three versus the Street's nine forty-three. Orders were up three point five percent year-over-year. Full-year sales guidance was trimmed slightly, but EPS guidance held. Mixed, with a quality beat on earnings offset by a revenue miss.

THOR Industries missed. Seventy-eight cents versus the Street's eighty-seven cents. Gross margins came in at twelve point four percent — down two hundred thirty basis points year-over-year and well below the thirteen point eight-five percent the Street expected. Management's language was cautious — stubborn rates, elevated fuel costs, inflationary pressure on household budgets. They're not giving formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. The bright spots were dealer inventory health and a seventy-five percent surge in North American towable RV order backlog. Still, this is a bearish print overall.

The biggest mover of the morning is Viking Therapeutics. Shares are spiking pre-market after positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735 showed twenty-two percent weight loss. That's a headline number that competes with the best in the class. This is a major catalyst — bullish and likely to move the broader GLP-1 space.

Finally, Pentair named a new CFO — Bob Hau, effective November first — with prior experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Transitional news, not a financial catalyst.

Bottom line for today: Viking is the name to watch on the GLP-1 theme, AutoZone's beat needs to be discounted for quality, and THOR's miss reflects ongoing consumer durables pressure. Stay sharp.
